description: Sync HubSpot CRM records and logged activities, with record-level permissions worked out from owners and teams.
intro: The HubSpot connector reads the CRM object types you select: deals, tickets, contacts and companies, and the notes, emails, calls, meetings and tasks logged on them. Each record or activity becomes one document.
Activities are linked to the deal, contact or company they are logged on. Records carry a list of who can read them, worked out from HubSpot owners and teams.

connect.auth: HubSpot uses an access token from a private app, or an OAuth access token.

credentials.name: access_token
credentials.text: A HubSpot private-app or OAuth access token. HydraDB does not refresh it, so a short-lived token must be replaced when it expires.

connect.permissions_label: Scopes for the app, all required

permissions.name: sales-email-read
permissions.text: email bodies. Without it, emails sync with their subject only.

permissions.name: crm.objects.owners.read
permissions.text: record owners, used to work out who can read a record.

permissions.name: settings.users.read
permissions.text: users, their teams and super-admin status, used for permissions.

steps.title: Create a private app
steps.text: In HubSpot, create a private app or an OAuth app that requests every scope above, and copy its access token.

steps.title: Select object types
steps.text: Discover lists the CRM object types the token can read. Select the ones to sync. Notes, emails, calls, meetings and tasks are offered only when the token can also read contacts, companies, deals and tickets.

steps.title: Name the roles that see everything
steps.text: When you configure the connector, list in `full_visibility_roles` the names of HubSpot roles whose members can see every record. HubSpot does not report what a role can see, so a member of such a role is otherwise not given access. Leaving the setting out keeps the current list; an empty list clears it.

shared_attributes.name: updated_at
shared_attributes.text: When the record was last modified. It is the document date, unless the activity has its own time. It is also in the text of notes and emails.

shared_attributes.name: created_at
shared_attributes.text: Used as the date only when there is no activity time and no modification time. It is also in the text of deals, tickets, notes, emails and calls.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.hubspot_id
shared_attributes.text: The HubSpot record id. Targets one record, and keeps later syncs on the same document.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.hubspot_object
shared_attributes.text: The object type, such as `deals` or `notes`. Limits a query to one type.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.rbac_warning
shared_attributes.text: Set when there was a problem working out who can read the record, such as readers that could not be resolved or a removed team. A warning does not by itself mean the record is public.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector.

shared_attributes.name: acl
shared_attributes.text: The people who can read the record, worked out as described under Permissions.

shared_attributes.name: object_type
shared_attributes.text: The object type the record came from. To filter on it, use `additional_metadata.hubspot_object`.

shared_attributes.name: Custom CRM properties
shared_attributes.text: Properties beyond the ones listed on this page are not kept.

documents.name: Deals
documents.title: The deal name.
documents.text: The deal description, then `Deal`, `Amount`, `Stage`, `Close date` and `Owner` lines.
documents.date: When the deal was last modified, else when it was created.

attributes.name: Deal text
attributes.text: The description and the lines described above.

attributes.name: title
attributes.text: Names the deal in results.

attributes.name: amount
attributes.text: Written as the `Amount` line.

attributes.name: close_date
attributes.text: Written as the `Close date` line.

attributes.name: stage
attributes.text: Written as the `Stage` line, as HubSpot's internal stage id, not its display name.

attributes.name: owner
purposes: Person or group in the graph
attributes.text: The owner's email, written as the `Owner` line. HydraDB can find the rep from that text. The owner is not declared as the deal's assignee.

attributes.name: pipeline
attributes.text: HubSpot's pipeline id. It is not turned into a name and is not searchable.

documents.name: Tickets
documents.title: The ticket subject.
documents.text: The ticket content. When the content is empty, the subject with `Priority` and `Stage` lines.
documents.date: When the ticket was last modified, else when it was created.

attributes.name: Ticket text
attributes.text: The content, or the fallback described above.

attributes.name: title
attributes.text: Names the ticket in results.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.text: Written as a `Priority` line.

attributes.name: stage
attributes.text: Written as a `Stage` line only when the ticket has no content. Otherwise it is stored and not searchable.

attributes.name: owner
attributes.text: The owner's email. It is not part of the text.

documents.name: Contacts and companies
documents.title: A contact's first and last name, else their email. A company's name.
documents.text: A contact: `Name`, `Email`, `Company`, `Phone` and `Job title` lines. A company: its description, then `Company`, `Domain` and `Industry` lines.
documents.date: When the record was last modified, else when it was created.

attributes.name: Contact or company text
attributes.text: The lines described above.

attributes.name: title
attributes.text: Names the contact or company in results.

attributes.name: email
attributes.text: A contact's email, so a query can find the person by email.

attributes.name: company
attributes.text: A contact's company name.

attributes.name: job_title
attributes.text: A contact's job title.

attributes.name: domain
attributes.text: A company's website domain, written as the `Domain` line.

attributes.name: industry
attributes.text: A company's industry, written as the `Industry` line.

attributes.name: company_id
attributes.text: Links a contact to its company's document.

attributes.name: owner
attributes.text: The owner's email. It is not part of the text.

documents.name: Notes
documents.title: Usually the first 80 characters of the note.
documents.text: The note body, converted from HTML to plain text.
documents.date: When the note was logged as happening, else when it was last modified, else when it was created.
documents.files: Files attached to the note are not synced.

attributes.name: Note text
attributes.text: The note body.

attributes.name: occurred_at
attributes.text: When the note was logged as happening. It is the document date.

attributes.name: owner
attributes.text: The owner's email. It is not part of the text.

documents.name: Emails
documents.title: The email subject.
documents.text: The plain-text body, else the HTML body converted to text, else the subject. The email's details, such as its direction, sender, recipient, owner and times, are written into the text as a list of fields.
documents.date: When the email happened, else when it was last modified, else when it was created.
documents.files: Files attached to the email are not synced.

attributes.name: Email text
attributes.text: The body and details described above.

attributes.name: title
attributes.text: The subject. Names the email in results.

attributes.name: from
purposes: Person or group in the graph
attributes.text: The sender. Part of the text, and attached to the email in the graph.

attributes.name: to
purposes: Person or group in the graph
attributes.text: The recipient. Part of the text, and attached to the email in the graph.

attributes.name: direction
attributes.text: Whether the email was inbound or outbound, written into the details.

attributes.name: owner
attributes.text: The owner's email, written into the details.

attributes.name: occurred_at
attributes.text: When the email happened. It is the document date, and it is written into the details.

documents.name: Calls
documents.title: Usually the first 80 characters of the call text, which include the call details.
documents.text: The call notes, converted from HTML, then `Call`, `Direction` and `Owner` lines.
documents.date: When the call happened, else when it was last modified, else when it was created.

attributes.name: Call text
attributes.text: The notes and lines described above.

attributes.name: direction
attributes.text: Written as the `Direction` line, so a query can match inbound or outbound calls.

attributes.name: owner
purposes: Person or group in the graph
attributes.text: Written as the `Owner` line. HydraDB can find the rep from that text.

attributes.name: occurred_at
attributes.text: When the call happened. It is the document date.

attributes.name: duration_ms
attributes.text: The call length in milliseconds. It is not searchable.

documents.name: Meetings and tasks
documents.one_document: One logged meeting, or one task.
documents.title: The meeting title, or the task subject.
documents.text: A meeting: its notes converted from HTML, then `Meeting`, `Location`, `Start` and `Owner` lines. A task: its body converted from HTML, then `Task`, `Status`, `Priority` and `Owner` lines.
documents.date: When the meeting or task happened, else when it was last modified, else when it was created.

attributes.name: Meeting or task text
attributes.text: The notes or body and the lines described above.

attributes.name: title
attributes.text: Names the meeting or task in results.

attributes.name: location
attributes.text: Where the meeting was held, written as the `Location` line.

attributes.name: start_time
attributes.text: When the meeting started, written as the `Start` line. The document date is the activity time.

attributes.name: status
attributes.text: A task's status, written as the `Status` line.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.text: A task's priority, written as the `Priority` line.

attributes.name: owner
purposes: Person or group in the graph
attributes.text: Written as the `Owner` line. HydraDB can find the rep from that text.

attributes.name: occurred_at
attributes.text: When the meeting or task happened. It is the document date.

attributes.name: end_time
attributes.text: When the meeting ended. It is not searchable and is not the document date.

connections: A note, email, call, meeting or task to the deal it is logged on. With no deal, to the contact. With no contact, to the company. When several records of one type are associated, the one with the lowest id is used.
An activity is linked to that record only if everyone who can read the activity can also read the record.
people: The record owner, as an email.
The sender and recipient of each email.
graph.from_text: Everything in deal descriptions, ticket content, and the text of notes, emails, calls, meetings and tasks.

permissions.who_can_read: Each deal, contact and company carries HubSpot's owners and the teams that can access it, including parent teams. Its readers are the owners, every member of those teams, every super admin, and the members of the roles you list in `full_visibility_roles`. An activity can be read by everyone who can read any record it is logged on. An activity logged on nothing uses its own owner and teams.
permissions.identity: A HubSpot user's or owner's email address.
permissions.when_unreadable: If a record names owners or teams but their readers cannot be worked out, the record gets an access warning, which you can find with `additional_metadata.rbac_warning`. An access rule you set stays in force. Without one, depending on your deployment's setting, the record is either readable by everyone or hidden until its readers can be worked out. A record with no owner or team information is not restricted and gets no warning.
notes: Tickets do not carry HubSpot's owner and team access lists, so owners and teams do not restrict them. Set an access rule on the tickets resource if tickets must be private.
Queues and archived owners give access to no one.
If an activity's parent record is not synced, the activity can be readable by everyone. Sync the deals, contacts and companies your activities are logged on.
This is HydraDB's reading of HubSpot owners, teams and roles. It is not a guarantee that HydraDB matches HubSpot's visibility in every case.

sync.first_sync: Each selected object type reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync reads records modified since the last sync. Owners, users and teams are read in full on every sync.
sync.edits: An edited record is read again and replaces its document.
sync.deletes: Deleted and archived HubSpot records are not removed. They stay in HydraDB.
notes: If the token lacks the scope for one object type, that type can be skipped while the others sync.

not_synced: Object types you did not select.
Email bodies, when the token lacks `sales-email-read`: those emails have their subject only.
Products, line items, quotes, forms, marketing emails and other HubSpot objects.
questions: What was said on the last call with this contact?
What amounts and close dates are recorded on the synced deals?
Which notes and emails are logged on the Acme deal?
What did the customer write in their last email?

good_to_know.title: Stages and pipelines are ids.
good_to_know.text: Deal stages appear in the text as HubSpot's internal ids, not their display names. Pipelines are not searchable.

good_to_know.title: Results do not link back to HubSpot.
good_to_know.text: No HubSpot URL is stored. Use `additional_metadata.hubspot_id` to find the record.

good_to_know.title: Older connectors sync every object type.
good_to_know.text: A connector set up before object types could be selected keeps syncing all of them until you configure it again.
